declarations.docstring: The left-derived functor of an additive functor is additive in every degree.
Deriving the sum of two natural transformations agrees with the sum of their derived transformations.
Mapping homological complexes sends the sum of natural transformations to the sum of the induced transformations.
The functor assigning projective resolutions is additive.
The morphism induced by a sum of linear maps is the sum of the induced morphisms.
The morphism induced by a composite of linear maps is the composite of the induced morphisms.
The identity linear map induces the identity morphism.
Canonical isomorphism between the derived object of a binary biproduct and the biproduct of the derived objects.
Canonical isomorphism between the derived object of a finite biproduct and the biproduct of the derived objects.
The displayed degreewise derived functor is additive.
Canonical isomorphism from the derived object formed with a finite family of modules to the corresponding biproduct.
Canonical isomorphism between the derived object for a product of two modules and the biproduct of the individual derived objects.
Constructs the morphism of derived objects induced by a linear map.
The derived morphism associated with a sum of linear maps is the sum of the associated morphisms.
The derived morphism associated with a composite of linear maps is the composite of the associated morphisms.
The identity linear map induces the identity morphism on the derived object.
The zero linear map induces the zero morphism on the derived object.
